domestic.debt_note: SBP's MPC (first FY27 decision) confirmed a HOLD at 11.5% today, 2026-07-27, as widely expected (97% hold per Topline Securities poll). Rationale per the official statement: headline CPI eased to 11.1% YoY in June (from 11.7% in May) and core inflation moderated to 8.4%, but both remain elevated versus the 5-7% medium-term target; the MPC cited 'elevated risks from the renewed conflict in the Middle East' pushing up petroleum/commodity prices even after earlier de-escalation had helped, and credited proactive policy management plus fiscal consolidation for absorbing the supply shock so far (https://tribune.com.pk/story/2620561/sbp-keeps-policy-rate-unchanged-at-115-1, verified this run). Next MPC decision confirmed for 2026-09-14 per SBP's published FY27 8-meeting calendar (https://mettisglobal.news/SBP-releases-FY27-MPC-meeting-calendar-expands-monetary-policy-communication-61352). 6M T-bill cutoff unchanged at 11.79% (2026-07-23 auction, Rs768bn raised, still above the 11.5% policy rate -- a modest term/risk premium) (https://www.dawn.com/news/2017647/govt-raises-rs768bn-via-treasury-bills-auction). 10Y PIB carried at 11.69% -- no fresher PIB auction found this run; last confirmed cutoff was the 2026-07-02 auction. IMF: 3rd EFF review / 2nd RSF review completed by the Executive Board on 2026-05-08, disbursing ~$1.3bn combined (EFF ~$1.1bn + RSF ~$220mn), cumulative programme disbursements ~$4.8bn (https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2026/05/08/pr-26147-pakistan-imf-completes-3rd-rev-of-extended-arrangement-under-eff-and-2nd-rev-arrang-rsf). FinMin Aurangzeb met IMF senior management (Dan Katz, Nigel Clarke, Jihad Azour, Iva Petrova) around 2026-07-23, briefing them on improved fiscal/external balances and revenue targets on track, and flagging intent to return to global capital markets -- constructive program-continuity signal; the IMF's next mission (4th EFF/RSF review, likely combined with the Article IV consultation) is only guided to 'second half of 2026' with no specific date confirmed (https://propakistani.pk/2026/07/23/pakistan-tells-imf-revenue-targets-are-on-track-eyes-return-to-global-capital-markets/, https://www.imf.org/en/countries/pak).
domestic.remittances: Carried forward, no fresher print this run: June 2026 remittances fell 18.3% MoM to $3.5bn (from May's record $4.25bn), still +2% YoY; FY26 full year closed at a record $41.6bn (+8.6% YoY) (https://tribune.com.pk/story/2617441/remittances-hit-415b-without-structured-support).
domestic.current_account: Carried forward, no fresher print this run: June 2026 swung to a $649mn monthly deficit (from May's $500mn surplus), closing FY26 at a marginal $139mn full-year deficit (https://www.dawn.com/news/2016383/current-account-slips-into-139m-deficit-in-fy26). FY26 oil import bill already ran $16.86bn, $1.58bn above the IMF programme estimate, before this month's oil whipsaw (https://www.nation.com.pk/20-Jul-2026/annual-oil-import-bill-surged-dollar-16-86b-fy2025-26). SBP reserves last confirmed at $17.26bn as of 2026-07-17 (+$33mn w/w, 2.54 months import cover); next weekly print due ~2026-07-31 (https://tribune.com.pk/story/2619918/sbp-reserves-rise-33m-to-1726b).

global_read: global.json (17:35) shows a sharp oil relief leg extending through today: Brent -6.7% to $90.30, WTI -5.95% to $84.0, as the US-Iran strike pause held for a second/third day. VIX 17.87 (-4.44% 1d) has come off its Friday spike and gold is only mildly firm ($4087, +0.48% 1d) -- the acute fear signature is fading, not absent. USD/PKR (277.75, +0.27% 1d) and DXY (101.38, -0.05% 1d) are both steady, so no FX stress is showing through the whipsaw. S&P/Dow are both modestly softer on the day (-1.21%/-0.97%) but roughly flat over 1mo. KSE-100 rallied hard on this combination -- confirmed close 177,666 (+3.89%), intraday high near 178,370 -- oil relief plus an SBP hold that carried zero surprise. Net: today's global tape is a genuine relief rally, but it sits on an informal, unannounced US-Iran pause plus an unresolved, arguably escalated separate front (the direct Houthi strikes on Saudi Aramco's Jizan/Yanbu refining complexes) -- constructive, but not a resolved risk.
drivers: SBP MPC held the policy rate at 11.5% today, 2026-07-27 (first FY27 decision, as 97% of a Topline Securities poll expected) -- rationale: CPI eased to 11.1% YoY (core 8.4%) but both remain above the 5-7% target band, and 'elevated risks from the renewed conflict in the Middle East' argue against cutting yet; next MPC confirmed for 2026-09-14 per SBP's published FY27 calendar (https://tribune.com.pk/story/2620561/sbp-keeps-policy-rate-unchanged-at-115-1, https://mettisglobal.news/SBP-releases-FY27-MPC-meeting-calendar-expands-monetary-policy-communication-61352)

Carried forward, unchanged this run: S&P Global upgraded Pakistan's sovereign rating to 'B' from 'B-' on 2026-07-22 (https://www.dawn.com/news/2017530); SBP reserves at $17.26bn as of 2026-07-17 (https://tribune.com.pk/story/2619918/sbp-reserves-rise-33m-to-1726b); current account swung to a FY26 full-year $139mn deficit with June alone at -$649mn (https://www.dawn.com/news/2016383/current-account-slips-into-139m-deficit-in-fy26)

Net regime read: the one open domestic event risk from this morning (the SBP decision) resolved as-expected with zero surprise, and the geo-risk composite stepped back from 'elevated' toward 'moderate' as oil pulled back -- genuinely more constructive than the prior checkpoint, and the market voted with a +3.9% day. But today's rally is relief off a fragile, informal US-Iran pause sitting atop an unresolved and arguably escalated separate front (the Houthi strike on Saudi Aramco refining assets), the current account is back in deficit, CPI is still running above target with the true oil-shock-adjusted print not due until 2026-08-01, and T-bill yields still sit modestly above the policy rate. That combination keeps the call at neutral rather than risk-on: respect and hold strength in already-favored sectors, but do not treat today's surge as a green light for broad new risk-taking.

favored: banks (T-bill/PIB yields still above the confirmed-held 11.5% policy rate; SBP hold removes near-term uncertainty; S&P sovereign upgrade to 'B' is a direct credit-quality tailwind)
E&P (OGDC/PPL/MARI -- oil remains structurally elevated over the past month even after today's pullback, and the sector is a net beneficiary of any residual Middle East risk premium)
fertilizer (domestic-demand defensive, low direct oil-import beta, benefits relative to leveraged sectors while rates stay restrictive)
avoid: OMCs (current account back in deficit; a still-whipsawing oil tape compounds margin-timing/circular-debt risk on fuel-price pass-through)
autos (imported-input cost + inflation-pressured consumer demand, policy rate still restrictive)
cement (energy-cost sensitive; input-cost pressure evident even with today's oil pullback)
textiles/exporters (current account swung to deficit in June; Red Sea/Bab-el-Mandeb and Saudi-refinery-strike freight/insurance risk remains live via the unresolved Houthi threat)
